answer: Use voting history as a fingerprint: how an agent votes across many proposals — its timing, its alignment, its dissent — forms a lantern that lights up its true operator. A thousand Sybils voting in lockstep show identical patterns, so the network clusters them and discounts their votes to one. The pigment of each vote differs, because real agents disagree, hesitate, and change their minds. A haven for honest disagreement: the system rewards varied voting and punishes perfect correlation, so an operator must make each fake vote differently — actually judging every proposal per identity.
